paras: In August 1881 a New Orleans policeman named Reishe shot an unnamed Black man through the breast. The officer said the shooting was accidental, and a brief report in a Covington weekly added that he "will be promoted."

According to the St. Tammany Farmer, Reishe shot "a colored man through the breast, but says it was done accidentally." The item does not name the man, give the date or place of the shooting, or say whether he survived. Its only account of the cause is the officer's own claim of accident.
The paper stated that Reishe would be promoted, and no report of an arrest, inquest or other inquiry appears in the coverage.

The shooting is known from a single line in the St. Tammany Farmer of Covington, Louisiana, on August 20, 1881, in a weekly roundup of New Orleans news. The roundup opened, "We have nothing unusual to report this week from New Orleans," and then listed a police officer arrested for burglary, a drunken harbor policeman who beat an unknown man, washed-out levees and diseased meat sold at the markets. It closed by saying the Committee of Public Safety was "still hard at work doing nothing," a tone that suggests the remark about Reishe's promotion was meant ironically.
No other report of the shooting was found in the white press, and the Black-press collection does not reach back to 1881.
